rubrics.description: Everything the answer must contain, one sentence each.
rubrics.title: Rubrics

CaseEvaluators.description:
Case's evaluator opt-ins: built-ins split into output and trajectory
families, plus opaque custom-evaluator blocks keyed by registered name.
CaseEvaluators.title: CaseEvaluators

name.description: Tool name, exactly as the trajectory records it.
name.title: Name

args_mode.description: subset: every expected key present and equal, extras allowed. exact: args equal. ignore: name alone. substring: like subset, but each expected value need only appear, case-insensitively, inside the actual value (lists and dicts compared as JSON text).
args_mode.title: Args Mode

match_overrides.description: Per-arg mode, overriding the one args_mode implies. Keys must be in args.
match_overrides.title: Match Overrides

MaxResponseTime.description: Wall-clock cap on the agent run.
MaxResponseTime.title: MaxResponseTime

OutputEvaluators.description: Evaluators that look only at the agent's returned output.
OutputEvaluators.title: OutputEvaluators

PresentationJudge.description:
Grades HOW the reply presents its information — units shown, columns
present, an artifact relayed rather than restated. Correctness of the
figures belongs to answer_rubrics; asserting the same thing in both places
reweights it rather than making the case stricter.

rubrics.description: The presentation properties this answer must satisfy. At least one must be a positive `rubric`.
rubrics.title: Rubrics

PresentationJudge.title: PresentationJudge

PresentationRubric.description: One property of how the reply presents its information.

rubric.description: A presentation property the answer must have. Write the property, not a description of the answer having it.
rubric.title: Rubric

forbid.description: A presentation property the answer must NOT have. Costs its points when violated; it does not zero the case.
forbid.title: Forbid

points.description: Weight of this rubric, relative within the case.
points.title: Points

note.description: Qualification of this rubric written by the case author, shown to the judge.
note.title: Note

PresentationRubric.title: PresentationRubric

RequiredToolsCalled.description: Tools the agent must call at least once. Scores the fraction called.
RequiredToolsCalled.title: RequiredToolsCalled

Rubric.description: One thing a correct answer contains, written as a sentence.

rubric.description: One assertion a correct answer contains, as a single sentence. Carries its own subject, period, unit and expected value — a figure with no stated band accepts normal roundings of itself; state a band only to tighten or widen that. Never names a tool, skill or data provider, and never refers to another rubric.
rubric.title: Rubric

type.description: Which kind of check this is; drives the per-type rates.
type.title: Type

source.description: The source the answer must credit this fact to, named at the level of detail the case cares about. Graded on its own citation axis. `factual_retrieval` only.
source.title: Source

Rubric.title: Rubric

ToolTrajectoryMatch.description:
Expected tool calls, matched by name and args, each against at most one
actual call. Scores the fraction found; `ordered` also requires them to
appear in this order.
ToolTrajectoryMatch.title: ToolTrajectoryMatch

TrajectoryEvaluators.description: Evaluators that look only at how the agent got to its output.
TrajectoryEvaluators.title: TrajectoryEvaluators

TrajectoryRubrics.description:
Checkpoints the recorded trajectory must show, one sentence each: an
intermediate value the derivation needs ("Retrieves FY2024 Platform revenue
as $3,522,776,000") or a process step in plain language ("Rounds the final
figure to the nearest basis point"). Order is not graded. By convention a
rubric never names a tool, skill or MCP server, so the case stays portable
across harnesses.
TrajectoryRubrics.title: TrajectoryRubrics
